passages.title: הַבֹּקֶר שֶׁל דָּנָה
passages.blurb: One morning, start to finish: the pa'al and hitpa'el present, the definite article, and telling the time.

passages.title: בַּשּׁוּק
passages.blurb: A shopping list at the market: numbers, quantities in smichut, יֵשׁ and אֵין, and this and that.

passages.title: הַחֶדֶר שֶׁל תֵּאוֹ
passages.blurb: One small room, from the window to under the bed: יֵשׁ and אֵין, place words, adjectives that agree, and the ownership endings.

passages.title: סוֹף הַשָּׁבוּעַ שֶׁל שָׂרָה
passages.blurb: A quiet Friday that does not stay quiet: the past tense in pa'al and in the other binyanim, הָיָה, the relative שֶׁ and the direction ־ָה.

passages.title: הַהוֹדָעָה
passages.blurb: A message from a number nobody knows: the future tense, the forms of a question, and the whole family of negative words.

passages.title: אֵצֶל הָרוֹפֵא
passages.blurb: A tired man, a waiting room and one awkward question: the negative words, יֵשׁ and אֵין, prepositions with endings, and the relative שֶׁ.

passages.title: הָרַכֶּבֶת הָאַחֲרוֹנָה
passages.blurb: A night train that will not leave, a father's old story, and a stranger who knew him. Past tense across the binyanim, the relative ש with the pronoun it leaves behind, and prepositions that decline.

passages.title: הַשּׁוּתָּפָה הַחֲדָשָׁה
passages.blurb: Two candidates for a spare room, one week of hesitating, and one phone call too late. אִם against אִילּוּ, the future tense inside a condition, and comparison with יוֹתֵר, פָּחוֹת and הֲכִי.

passages.title: רֵאָיוֹן הָעֲבוֹדָה
passages.blurb: A job interview held in two Hebrews at once: the formal one spoken out loud, and the blunt one kept inside the head. Register from הִנְּךָ מִתְבַּקֵּשׁ to סַבַּבָּה, the passive binyanim, and clauses of contrast and purpose.

passages.title: הַמִּכְתָּב מִשְּׁנַת 1974
passages.blurb: An unsent letter in the bottom drawer, written in a Hebrew nobody speaks, and a second handwriting at the foot of the last page. Possessive endings against שֶׁל, אֲשֶׁר for שֶׁ, the passive binyanim, and reporting speech without shifting the tense.

passages.title: א. הַיְרוּשָּׁה
passages.blurb: Chapter one of ten. A lawyer's letter reaches Haifa about a great-aunt Ido had almost forgotten: the past tense in pa'al and in the other binyanim, possession with שֶׁל, and the relative שֶׁ.

passages.title: ב. הַדִּירָה
passages.blurb: Chapter two of ten. Ido climbs up to the flat that is now his, and someone opens the door from the inside: direction and place, prepositions that decline in the plural, and weak roots on the move.

passages.title: ג. הַשְּׁכֵנָה
passages.blurb: Chapter three of ten. Over two cups of coffee a stranger describes the aunt Ido never knew: habitual past, the relative שֶׁ doing the joining, and comparison with יוֹתֵר מִ and פָּחוֹת מִ.

passages.title: ד. מַה שֶּׁהִיא עָשְׂתָה
passages.blurb: Chapter four of ten. A lawyer lays out a document signed in 1998 and the inheritance changes shape: dates and ordinals, numbers past a hundred, verbal nouns, and reporting what someone said.

passages.title: ה. אִלּוּ הָיִיתִי יוֹדֵעַ
passages.blurb: Chapter five of ten. Ido and his sister argue about money down a bad phone line: אִם for what may happen, אִלּוּ plus הָיָה for what did not, and the future tense that goes with them.

passages.title: ו. מַה שֶּׁצָּרִיךְ
passages.blurb: Chapter six of ten. A lawyer lists what Ido is permitted to do, and his mother tells him what he is not obliged to understand: obligation and permission with צָרִיךְ, חַיָּיב, מוּתָּר, אָסוּר and כְּדַאי plus the infinitive, and purpose clauses with כְּדֵי and כְּדֵי שֶׁ.

passages.title: ז. קוּפְסַת הַפַּח
passages.blurb: Chapter seven of ten. Pnina opens a biscuit tin of unanswered letters and thirty years get reported second hand: אָמַר שֶׁ, שָׁאַל אִם, and the tense Hebrew does not push back.

passages.title: ח. מַה שֶּׁאַף אֶחָד לֹא דִּיבֵּר עָלָיו
passages.blurb: Chapter eight of ten. The one reply the grandmother did send, read out loud at last: the relative ש with the pronoun it leaves behind, and the prepositions that decline in the plural.

passages.title: ט. הִיא חָשְׁבָה עַל הַכֹּל
passages.blurb: Chapter nine of ten. A second letter comes out of the lawyer's drawer and Ido works out what Odelya arranged: the future used for guessing, the passive binyanim on the documents, and clauses of time.

passages.title: י. לְאַט לְאַט
passages.blurb: Chapter ten of ten. A year of Fridays, one signature, and a paragraph in an old book: durations with בְּמֶשֶׁךְ, מֵאָז, לִפְנֵי and כְּבָר, and a closing page that climbs into a higher, almost biblical register.
